suggestions.title: Partial Differential Equations
suggestions.description_md:
The mathematics of fields that vary in space and time — heat diffusing
through a metal bar, waves spreading on a drum head, the electrostatic
potential around a charge, the Schrödinger evolution of a quantum state.
Builds the classification into hyperbolic, parabolic, and elliptic
equations, the canonical solution techniques (separation of variables,
Fourier methods, Green's functions, method of characteristics), and the
qualitative differences in behaviour each class produces.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Builds on the ODEs you're refreshing; essential for modeling spatiotemporal dynamics in neural systems.

suggestions.title: Complex Analysis
suggestions.description_md:
The calculus of functions of a complex variable, where the constraint
of differentiability is so strong it forces analytic functions to be
uniquely determined by their values on any small disk. Builds toward
contour integration, the residue theorem, and the deep connection
between the complex plane and physics — conformal maps in fluid
dynamics, Cauchy's integral formula as a tool throughout theoretical
physics, and analytic continuation as a window onto the structure of
special functions.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Underpins Fourier methods and linear stability analysis—tools you'll need for dynamical systems theory.

suggestions.title: Real Analysis
suggestions.description_md:
The rigorous foundations of calculus — sequences, limits, continuity,
differentiation, and integration developed from first principles via
ε-δ arguments. Where calculus teaches you to compute, real analysis
teaches you to prove, building toward metric spaces, uniform
convergence, and the Lebesgue integral. The discipline behind why the
manipulations you've been doing actually work.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Rigorous foundation for the probability and measure theory that information theory rests on.
